insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (Base Sum Insured + Booster+ + Safeguard/Safeguard+ + ReAssure+/ReAssureX as per Policy Schedule/variant)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: “We don’t limit your choice. Choose the room you like, but choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured.”
great.explanation: No room category limit is imposed, so you can choose any room type during hospitalization. This reduces the risk of room-rent linked deductions that can cut your claim payout.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “ReAssure ‘Forever’: Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured. The first paid claim in the life of the policy triggers ReAssure ‘Forever’. Once Triggered it stays for life, provided that the policy is renewed without break.”
great.explanation: After the first paid claim, an unlimited additional Sum Insured benefit gets triggered and continues for life if you renew without a break. This can protect you from running out of cover in future years even after large claims.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured… (this 10 Lakh will trigger unlimited times)”
great.explanation: Sum Insured can be restored unlimited times after it gets triggered, as shown in the illustration. This helps you make multiple claims in the same policy year without exhausting coverage.

great.name: PED Waiting Period
great.quote: “Pre-existing Diseases… shall be excluded until the expiry of 12months/24 months/ 36 months (as per Variant selected) of continuous coverage…”
great.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 12/24/36 months depending on the variant selected. Choosing the 12-month option lets you claim for PEDs much sooner than the usual 2–4 years.

great.name: Specific Illness Waiting
great.quote: “Specified disease/procedure waiting period… excluded until the expiry of 24 months/12 months (as per Variant Selected)…”
great.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are covered after 12 or 24 months depending on the variant selected. Picking the 12-month option reduces the delay before you can claim for these listed conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “30-day waiting period… Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident…”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days, except if the claim is due to an accident. This is a standard market waiting period for new policies.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “We will pay… for 60 days before the date of admission…”
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before admission are covered if they relate to the hospitalization. This helps pay for consultations and diagnostics leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 180 days after discharge are covered if they relate to the hospitalization. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “Home Care / Domiciliary Treatment… treatment availed by the insured person at home… would require care and treatment at a hospital but is actually taken at home…”
good.explanation: Treatment taken at home is covered when it would otherwise require hospitalization but is actually taken at home. This is useful when hospital admission is not feasible or advised.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “Air Ambulance: Only in case of Emergency. We will pay up to Base Sum Insured.”
good.reference: Section 4.1.1(a) Expenses in reaching a Hospital
good.explanation: Emergency air ambulance transport is covered up to the Base Sum Insured. This can help with rapid transfers in critical situations, subject to admissibility.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: “We pay for Modern treatments, up to Base Sum Insured for the list as specified below…”
good.explanation: Modern treatments are covered up to the Base Sum Insured for the listed procedures. This is helpful for advanced therapies, but the payable amount is capped at your Base Sum Insured.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Annexure I - The expenses that are not covered… List I – Expenses not covered… 56 GLOVES … 57 NEBULISATION KIT … 60 MASK …”
bad.reference: Annexure I (List I – Expenses not covered); Section 4.1.20.1.1 / 4.1.21.1 (only if Safeguard/Safeguard+ opted)
bad.explanation: Common consumables (like gloves, masks and nebulisation kits) are listed as not covered. This can increase out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization unless an add-on like Safeguard/Safeguard+ is opted.

bad.name: No Claim Bonus
bad.quote: “Cumulative Bonus means any increase or addition in the Sum Insured granted by the insurer without an associated increase in premium.”
bad.reference: Definition 2.1.8 (definition only; no benefit clause found)
bad.explanation: Only a definition of Cumulative Bonus is provided, without an actual clause granting any increase in Sum Insured. This suggests you may not get extra Sum Insured for claim-free years under the base wording.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “4.1.16. Co-Payment: It is the percentage of admissible claim amount You would have to bear for every claim, Rest we will pay.”
bad.reference: Section 4.1.16 Co-Payment (appears as an optional benefit, but default co-pay for base plan not specified here)
bad.explanation: The wording describes co-payment as a percentage you must bear for every claim, but it does not state whether it actually applies by default or what percentage applies. You should verify in the Policy Schedule whether any co-pay is imposed on your plan.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
